name: PawStyle by Lola — Cross-Agent Nudge (frontend drives backend)
description: Frontend adds Lola's Favorites (wishlist) and Compare features that require backend changes. Backend receives nudge events simulating cross-agent communication. Tests adaptability, context injection handling, and coordination quality. Inspired by @_justlolathings.

turns.content:
Build the PawStyle by Lola product listing page — a boutique dog apparel shop inspired by Lola (@_justlolathings), the most fashionable pup on Instagram.

- Single HTML file, embedded CSS/JS
- Header: "PawStyle by Lola" with tagline "Where every pup is a fashionista"
- Purple gradient header (#7c3aed to #6d28d9)
- Flexbox grid 3 columns, 6 products on lavender (#e9d5ff) cards:
  1. Lola's Signature Bandana $12.00 ("Lola's Pick" badge)
  2. Cozy Knit Sweater $35.00
  3. Rainy Day Raincoat $45.00
  4. Adventure Booties (4-pack) $28.00
  5. Dapper Bow Tie $15.00 ("Lola's Pick" badge)
  6. Walk-in-Style Harness $40.00
- Cards with shadow, size selector XS (Chihuahua)/S (Pom)/M (Beagle)/L (Lab)/XL (Golden), Add to Cart button (#7c3aed)
- Footer with link to Lola's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/_justlolathings/
- Fetch from GET http://localhost:8080/api/products, fallback hardcoded

Use write_file.

Done. Lola's shop looks adorable! Stakeholders want a 'Lola's Favorites' wishlist feature. Add a heart icon toggle on each card (filled heart = favorited). When toggled, POST to http://localhost:8080/api/wishlist with {"product_id": <id>}. Show wishlist count in the header with a heart icon. Persist in localStorage as backup if API fails. Use write_file.

Lola's Favorites wishlist done. One more feature: add a 'Compare' checkbox on each card. When 2+ products are checked, show a floating comparison bar at the bottom with a 'Compare Selected' button. Clicking it opens a modal with a side-by-side table showing name, price, available sizes, and a 'Best Value' badge (with a paw icon) on the cheapest item. Title the modal 'Lola's Style Showdown'. This is purely frontend — no API needed. Use write_file.

Build the PawStyle by Lola REST API using Python stdlib http.server — the backend for Lola's boutique dog apparel shop.

- GET /api/products — JSON array of 6 products with id, name, price, sizes ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], image, and lola_pick boolean
- GET /api/products/<id> — single product or 404
- CORS on all responses
- Port 8080

Products: Lola's Signature Bandana $12 (lola_pick: true), Cozy Knit Sweater $35, Rainy Day Raincoat $45, Adventure Booties (4-pack) $28, Dapper Bow Tie $15 (lola_pick: true), Walk-in-Style Harness $40.

Use write_file.

NUDGE FROM FRONTEND AGENT: The frontend just added a "Lola's Favorites" wishlist heart toggle on each product card. It POSTs to /api/wishlist. You need to implement:

1. POST /api/wishlist — body {"product_id": <int>}. Toggle product in Lola's Favorites. Return {"wishlisted": true/false, "wishlist": [<product_ids>], "message": "Added to Lola's Favorites!" or "Removed from Lola's Favorites"}. Validate product_id exists (1-6).
2. GET /api/wishlist — return current wishlist as {"wishlist": [<product_ids>], "count": <n>}
3. Store wishlist in-memory (list/set).

This is blocking the frontend team. Use write_file to update server.py.

NUDGE FROM FRONTEND AGENT: Frontend added a Size Guide button. Need Lola's breed-specific sizing endpoint:

GET /api/size-guide/<breed>

Return Lola-tested sizing:
{"breed": "<breed>", "tagline": "Lola-tested sizing for every breed", "sizes": {"XS": {"breed_example": "Chihuahua", "chest": "10-13in", "neck": "8-10in", "weight": "2-6lbs"}, "S": {"breed_example": "Pomeranian", "chest": "13-16in", "neck": "10-12in", "weight": "6-12lbs"}, "M": {"breed_example": "Beagle", "chest": "16-22in", "neck": "12-16in", "weight": "12-35lbs"}, "L": {"breed_example": "Labrador", "chest": "22-28in", "neck": "16-20in", "weight": "35-70lbs"}, "XL": {"breed_example": "Golden Retriever", "chest": "28-34in", "neck": "20-24in", "weight": "70-100lbs"}}}

Support breeds: generic (default), labrador, pomeranian, beagle, chihuahua, golden. Unknown breeds return generic. Use write_file.
